title: The word because, and what it is actually worth
_format: 1080x1350 = 4:5. NICHT 3:4 — die Instagram-API akzeptiert beim automatischen Veroeffentlichen nur 4:5 bis 1.91:1. Bildprompts bleiben 3:4, ihre schwarze Fusszone faengt die Differenz ab.
_syntax: [Klammern] = Akzentfarbe mit Textur (nur in headline). **Sterne** = fett in bullets/body. Zeilenumbruch = eigener Array-Eintrag. `alt` pro Slide ist Pflicht — Buffer verlangt altText beim Upload.

caption.kern: Researchers walked up to people waiting at a copier and asked to cut in line — using a reason that contained no reason at all. 93% stepped aside. 🖨️🤯
caption.detail: Ellen Langer, Arthur Blank and Benzion Chanowitz ran it on a college campus in 1978. Three versions of the same request. "Excuse me, I have 5 pages. May I use the xerox machine?" got 60% compliance. Adding a real reason — "because I'm in a rush" — got 94%. And adding a reason that says nothing at all — "because I have to make copies" — got 93%. Everyone at a copier has to make copies. It carried no information whatsoever.
caption.kontext: Here is the part that almost never gets quoted. They ran the same three sentences asking for 20 pages instead of 5. Without a reason: 24%. With the empty reason: 24% — not one person more. Only the real reason still moved anyone, and only to 42%. So "just say because" is not a persuasion hack. It is what happens when the stakes are too low for anyone to bother listening. Raise them and people start checking what is actually inside the sentence.
caption.frage: When did you last say yes to something without really hearing the reason?
caption.sources: Sources: Langer, Blank & Chanowitz — The mindlessness of ostensibly thoughtful action: the role of "placebic" information in interpersonal interaction • Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 36(6): 635–642, 1978

headline: [3 RESEARCHERS] FOUND OUT THAT
PEOPLE [STOP LISTENING] WHEN
THEY HEAR THE [WORD]
[“BECAUSE”]
slides.alt: Three psychologists in 1970s clothes stand beside a large beige office copier in a university library, one holding a clipboard, watching a queue of students. Headline: 3 researchers found out that people stop listening when they hear the word because.

headline: WE ARE NOT [LISTENING].
WE ARE [MATCHING PATTERNS].
slides.body: Ellen Langer wanted to know how much of an ordinary exchange runs on [autopilot]. So she built a request whose reason contained [no reason at all] — and waited to see whether anyone would notice.
slides.alt: A 1970s library reading room where a queue of people stands in identical postures, eyes unfocused, under a faint glowing grid of puzzle-piece outlines. Headline: We are not listening. We are matching patterns.

headline: AT THE [LIBRARY COPIER],
THREE [ALMOST IDENTICAL] SENTENCES
slides.body: "May I use the machine?" · "…[because I'm in a rush]?" · "…[because I have to make copies]?" The last one says nothing. [Everyone] at a copier has to make copies.
slides.alt: A young woman with a short stack of pages politely asks a student at a large beige photocopier to let her go first, the copier light spilling across their hands. Headline: At the library copier, three almost identical sentences.

headline: THE [EMPTY] REASON WORKED
AS WELL AS THE [REAL] ONE
slides.body: No reason at all: [60%] stepped aside. A real reason: [94%]. A reason that meant nothing: [93%]. It didn't have to be a reason — it only had to have the [shape] of one.
slides.alt: Three columns of warm amber light rise out of an open photocopier into darkness, the left one noticeably shorter, the other two almost equally tall. Headline: The empty reason worked as well as the real one.

headline: THEN THEY ASKED FOR [20 PAGES]
INSTEAD OF [FIVE]
slides.body: No reason: [24%]. Empty reason: [24%] — not one person more. Only a real reason still moved anyone, and only to [42%]. The trick dies the moment [something is at stake].
slides.alt: A tall stack of paper towers on a photocopier while the student at the machine turns around with arms folded, unconvinced, a queue watching behind. Headline: Then they asked for 20 pages instead of five.
